name: tintin
why: A decades-old MUD client with its own scripting language, a strange old-school environment worth an afternoon.

brief.what_it_is: TinTin++ (tt++) is a free MUD client, a terminal program for connecting to text-based multiplayer games (MUDs). The homepage says it runs on Android, iOS, Linux, Mac OS X and Windows. It takes a connection to a MUD server and shows the text in a VT100 terminal interface, with an automapper and a built-in scripting language for triggers, aliases, highlights, timers and similar automation. The homepage also says it can act as a Unix shell command language and a multiplexer that runs other console programs, such as bash, inside the client.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a full-featured MUD client with an advanced automapper, scripting language and VT100 interface, and says it is designed to be accessible: it is a non-graphical command interface that works with screen readers.
brief.how_it_works: Programs and scripts are written in the tt++ scripting language, which the homepage describes as a fast built-in engine using just-in-time compilation. Triggers and other rules can use Perl-compatible regular expressions, and the client can split the screen, divert text to subwindows and run other command-line programs such as ssh or sftp with full access to the scripting language.

commands_seen.context: Opens TinTin++'s internal help files; the homepage points users to this alongside the manual.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists Homebrew as the easy route on Mac OS X. Linux and Unix users can compile from source, which the homepage says works on most systems and under Cygwin. Windows has the WinTin++ port, which uses the PuTTY-derived mintty terminal and is offered as an installer; the page says it runs on Windows XP through 10 and is for people not using Cygwin. Android and ChromeOS need Termux, and iPhone/iPad need iSH. The homepage also mentions running an ssh daemon on a Mac, Linux or Unix machine for remote access to the client.
brief.standout: It is a MUD client that doubles as a general-purpose scripting and multiplexing environment for console programs, with its own scripting language and built-in automapper. The homepage also stresses screen-reader accessibility, which is less common in terminal tools of this kind.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage shows no release date or last-commit date, and it links to a GitHub forum and Discord for support. The Windows version list (XP through 10) suggests the page itself may be dated, but I could not confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The Windows port is WinTin++ rather than the main client, and the page's Windows support list is old. Android, ChromeOS and iOS require third-party terminal environments (Termux or iSH). The homepage does not name a license. I did not check the GitHub README or the manual, so details beyond the homepage are unverified.
quotes: TinTin++ (aka tt++) is a free Mud client for Android, iOS, Linux, Mac OS X and Windows.
While TinTin++ is primarily a Mud client it can be used as a Unix shell command language, multiplexer/demultiplexer and automator.
Installation on Mac OS X is easy by using the Homebrew package installer.

judge.reason: TinTin++ pairs a MUD client and automapper with its own scripting language, and can multiplex ordinary console programs—a distinctive terminal environment beyond a typical game client.

entry.title: TinTin++
entry.tldr: A terminal client for MUDs, the text-based multiplayer games, with a built-in scripting language for triggers, aliases, timers and an automapper.
entry.deeper_look:
TinTin++ (tt++) connects to MUD servers and shows their text in a VT100 terminal interface. MUDs are multiplayer worlds that run entirely as text. The client sits between you and the server and can rewrite, react to and automate what passes through.

The automation is the interesting part. tt++ has its own scripting language for triggers, aliases, highlights and timers. Triggers can match with Perl-compatible regular expressions. The homepage describes the engine as fast, with just-in-time compilation. It also includes an automapper that builds a map of the world as you move through it, and it can split the screen and divert text into subwindows.

The homepage says that, although it is primarily a MUD client, it can also be used as a Unix shell command language and as a multiplexer that runs other console programs such as bash, ssh or sftp inside the client, with full access to the scripting language. So the same idea of pattern-matching on a text stream and reacting to it applies to a shell session as much as to a dungeon.

The homepage also stresses accessibility. It is a non-graphical command interface that works with screen readers.
entry.install:
brew install tintin
# the executable is tt++

try_this.what_happens: Prints the command-line options for the client.
Starts the client at its prompt, where you can type commands and scripts.
Typed inside tt++, opens the built-in help files.

entry.whats_unique: It is a MUD client that doubles as a general scripting and multiplexing environment for console programs. It also has a built-in automapper and a stated focus on screen-reader accessibility.
entry.caveats: The homepage shows no release dates, so recent activity is unconfirmed, and its Windows support list (XP through 10) looks dated.
